title: HDFC Bank Taps ICICI's Anup Bagchi as CEO With Stock Down 27% in 2026
excerpt: RBI approved Anup Bagchi's appointment as MD and CEO for a three-year term from October 27, 2026, ending months of succession uncertainty. Jefferies reaffirmed HDFC Bank as its top Indian pick with a Rs 880 target, even as the stock sits 27% below its 2025 close.
body:
• HDFC Bank has named Anup Bagchi as its next Managing Director and CEO for a three-year term starting October 27, 2026, after the Reserve Bank of India approved the appointment on October 1. He succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends October 26.
  • The stock closed at ₹721.20 on October 1 — down 25.3% from a year earlier and 27.2% in 2026 so far. Analysts identify ₹700 as the key support level, with stronger support around ₹650.
  • What it means for investors: Jefferies reaffirmed HDFC Bank as its top pick among Indian equities with a ₹880 price target (about 22% upside) and a $28 ADR target, saying the end of succession uncertainty removes a key overhang. Consult a SEBI-registered adviser before acting.
  • Bagchi, a 30-plus-year ICICI Group veteran and current MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life, becomes HDFC Bank's first external CEO. ICICI Prudential named Siddhartha Mishra as his successor, effective October 14.

HDFC Bank has appointed Anup Bagchi as its next Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, ending months of uncertainty over succession at India's largest private-sector lender. The bank said in an exchange filing on October 1 that the Reserve Bank of India approved Bagchi's appointment under Section 35B of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, for a three-year term beginning October 27, 2026. The appointment is subject to shareholder approval, and Bagchi joins the board as an Additional Director on October 2.

Bagchi succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, who completes his tenure at the close of business on October 26 after deciding not to seek another term. The bank's board sent two ranked candidates to the RBI last month; the regulator's approval of Bagchi on October 1 closed the process.

Context and Background

The leadership change arrives after a punishing run for the stock. HDFC Bank closed at ₹721.20 on October 1, against ₹965.25 a year earlier (down 25.3%) and ₹991.20 at end-2025 (down 27.2% in 2026). The stock hit a 52-week low of ₹681.90 in the week of September 7.

The decline reflects several forces: net interest margin slipped to 3.26% in Q1 FY27, foreign investors cut their holding from 48.61% to 41.83%, and the bank is still digesting its 2023 merger with HDFC Ltd, which built a much larger franchise with a heavy mortgage book. The valuation has compressed accordingly — from 3.5 to 4.2 times price-to-book historically to roughly 2.37 times now.

The underlying business is not broken. Q1 FY27 net profit rose 5% year on year to ₹19,060 crore and net interest income grew 6.7% to ₹33,535 crore, with deposits above ₹31.7 lakh crore, gross NPAs at 1.17% and capital adequacy at 19.6%.

Impact and Analysis

Bagchi is unusual for HDFC Bank: its first external CEO. He has been with the ICICI Group since 1992 — Executive Director of ICICI Bank from 2017 to 2023, where the retail mortgage portfolio crossed ₹2 lakh crore, then MD and CEO of ICICI Securities, and since June 2023 MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. In FY25 the insurer crossed ₹10,000 crore in annualised premium equivalent for the first time, with APE up 15% to ₹10,407 crore and profit after tax up nearly 40% to ₹1,189 crore.

"From a technical perspective, the stock is trading close to a key support zone. The ₹700 level is likely to act as an important support, followed by stronger support around ₹650."

— Anuj Gupta, SEBI-registered Research Analyst

Jefferies India's response was swift: it reaffirmed HDFC Bank as its top pick among Indian equities with a "Buy" rating and a ₹880 target — roughly 22% upside — alongside a $28 target for the NYSE-listed ADR. Jefferies argued that confirming an external candidate ends months of succession uncertainty and that smooth continuity could catalyse a valuation rerating across private banking.

The US market reacted positively: HDFC Bank's ADR rose 4.12% in pre-market trading and closed 2.73% higher at $22.95 on October 1, though it remains well below its 52-week high of $37.45.

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, this story runs through portfolios. HDFC Bank's ADR (NYSE: HDB) and Indian banking ETFs are common diaspora holdings, and the 27% slide in 2026 has hurt. An external CEO with a retail-franchise record offers a credible reset narrative — but one-day ADR pops do not establish a trend, and an outsider restructuring a bank of this scale carries real execution risk.

What's Next

Watch Bagchi's first statements on deposit growth, CASA, margins and the mortgage book, plus Q2 FY27 results for signs the operating metrics behind the cheap valuation are stabilising. On the charts, analysts say a sustained hold above ₹700 would confirm the market is giving the new CEO the benefit of the doubt.
